title: The news
hook: read the news and pray for the people in it
tomorrow: a stranger online calls Sofia trash. what does she type back?

segments.voice: Yesterday, social media: only what builds up the hearers, and a pause long enough to see the person. The line was would he post it.

A push alert at lunch. Another at dinner. A flood somewhere, a fire somewhere else, faces on a screen for a few seconds and then gone. Two easy responses: go numb, or stop looking. Some grandmothers have a third. They watch the evening news with a rosary in hand, praying for whoever comes on the screen. Does it help anyone? The question underneath is older: who are those people to me?
screen: `A FLOOD, A FIRE, GONE.` → `NUMB, OR LOOK AWAY?` → `A ROSARY THROUGH THE NEWS.`

segments.voice: The Second Vatican Council opened one of its documents with an answer. The joys and hopes, the griefs and anxieties of people today, especially the poor and all who suffer, are the joys and hopes, the griefs and anxieties of the followers of Christ. Nothing truly human, it says, fails to echo in their hearts. Another Council document starts from the other end: all peoples are one community, with one origin, because God made the whole human race. So the people in the headline aren't strangers. They're family, a long way off. Paul gives the picture, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "if one member suffer any thing, all the members suffer with it." Praying the news is letting that ache in and turning it toward God, and sometimes toward a gift or a hand. A neighbor tradition uses nearly the same picture. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is reported in a hadith to have said that believers, in their love, mercy and kindness to one another, are like one body: when one part aches, the whole body answers with sleeplessness and fever. Catholics and Muslims share that image of a body that can't rest while one part hurts. The difference is honest. Paul's body is the body of Christ, which Catholics believe is joined to Christ himself; the hadith speaks of the believers' mercy to one another, with no such claim. Neither ranks anyone. Both refuse to look away.
screen: `JOYS AND HOPES, GRIEFS AND ANXIETIES.` · `ONE COMMUNITY, ONE ORIGIN.` · `ALL THE MEMBERS SUFFER WITH IT.` · `LIKE ONE BODY, IN FEVER.` · then, large: `PRAY THE NEWS.`

segments.voice: Open one headline, or bring back one you saw today, and rest your eyes on a single face or place in it. Stay there for a few breaths, as if it were family a long way off. If you pray, you can pray for them by name or by place; if not, simply hold them in mind.
The news. The day's headlines, read as news about family: the people in them, held in prayer.
Your line: pray the news. The people in the headline belong to one human family. Peace to you.

howItsDone: Catholics pray for the world in the prayers of the faithful at Mass, and some keep a habit of praying for the people in the day's news, often with the rosary.

fork.setup: a classmate scrolls past a story about families fleeing a war and says 'not my problem, I don't know them.' what's today's answer?
options: the Church calls all peoples one community, with one origin.
he has a point; prayer is mostly for the people close to you.
only people who share one faith are really connected.
fork.reveal: Nostra Aetate: one community, one origin. Gaudium et Spes: the griefs of people today are the griefs of Christ's followers. family, a long way off.

original.note: Latin: joy and hope. the first words, and the name, of the Council's document on the Church in the world today.

trapdoor: what you thought: praying for the news is a way to feel better about not helping.
what it means: holding the people in the headlines before God as members of one human family.
what a scholar hears: Gaudium et Spes 1 and Nostra Aetate 1 frame the human race as one community, beside Paul's one body in 1 Corinthians 12.
guess: the day's headlines, read as family news
a report on church events only

chat.says: abuela prays her rosary through the whole news. ok but does praying for strangers actually do anything?
options: It stops them being strangers. One body: when one part hurts, the rest won't look away.
Not really. Prayer is for people you know; strangers have their own families.
Only if they're Catholic too. Prayer works for members of the Church.
chat.meaning: The Council says the griefs of people today are the griefs of Christ's followers. One body: when one member suffers, all suffer with it.

Second Vatican Council.meaning: a council of the world's Catholic bishops that renewed the Church

hadith.meaning: a reported saying or action of the Prophet Muhammad

rosary.meaning: a prayer counted on beads, meditating on Jesus and Mary

sources.work: Second Vatican Council, Gaudium et Spes

sources.quoted: if one member suffer any thing, all the members suffer with it

notes: Douay-Rheims 1 Corinthians 12:26 quoted from memory; confirm exact Challoner wording.

Gaudium et Spes 1 paraphrased (the joys and hopes, the griefs and anxieties of the men of this age, especially those who are poor or in any way afflicted, are the joys and hopes, the griefs and anxieties of the followers of Christ; nothing genuinely human fails to raise an echo in their hearts). Confirm.
Nostra Aetate 1 paraphrased (one community, one origin, for God made the whole human race to live over the face of the earth). This carries the 'one human race' thread the owner asked for. Confirm.

v3 unity thread (wisdom day): hadith of the one body (Sahih Muslim 2586; cf. Bukhari 6011) paraphrased, not quoted (English hadith translations are under copyright). Shared ground: one body that aches together. Honest difference: Paul's body is the body of Christ (Catholic belief); the hadith speaks of believers' mercy to one another. Please have a Muslim reader confirm the paraphrase, the honorific, and that the framing is fair.
Hook: 'some grandmothers ... watch the evening news with a rosary in hand' is a general image, not a statistic.
Practice kind: look at one object (one face or place in a headline). The once-a-week 'if you pray...; if not...' form is used here.
